- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.40), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., > +1.5% from prior day), model often overshoots downward; reduce forecast dip by 0.5–1.0% to account for momentum lag.  
- If recent 3–5 day mean reversion is strong (e.g., 3 consecutive days below 60), model underreacts; add 0.3–0.7% upward bias to avoid mean-reversion underestimation.  
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (e.g., 0.0 to +0.30), model often underestimates upside; add 0.2–0.5% upward adjustment to capture sentiment-driven momentum.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently underestimates late-period (last 7–10 days) price action; apply 0.5–1.0% upward bias to the final 5–7 days to reflect sentiment-driven volatility.
